result.paraphrase: Web browsing is a key requirement for Internet users. Because current mobile Web apps can include computation-intensive JavaScript logic, browsing performance can suffer. Drawing on more than a decade of research and development in the Internetware paradigm, we introduce the novel, general i-Jacob approach for improving mobile Web browsing performance through effective JavaScript-code offloading. It offers a programming abstraction that makes mobile Web operation situational and context-adaptive by identifying computation-intensive and “offloadable” code, and it builds a platform-independent lightweight runtime that spans mobile devices and the cloud. We show i-Jacob’s efficiency using typical computation-intensive tasks across varied hardware, operating systems, browsers, and network connections. The gains can reach up to 49× faster response times and 90% energy savings.
